stage: S2 conditional development diagnostic; no dated-role calibration or production qualification
question: Does the existing environmental/centre-intensity model distinguish recorded nucleated contexts from recorded farm/villa contexts within the excavated archive, without using unsurveyed space as absence?
known_before_plan: All source observations already exposed through preparation. Initial schemas and full-source class counts inspected:527records have a nucleated minor label,2207farm/villa,23overlap. Requiring DOMESTIC_OCCUPATION=Yes and exclusive class labels gives426nucleated-only and2049farm/villa-only records. Existing Rome input keys/shapes inspected; no source-to-grid matching, role-contrast predictor scores or AUC computed. Earth city pools remain exposed; this is not blind.
source: Pinned five-table rural-Britain snapshot plus original Roman400x600 Earth input, using its existing source hashes. Preserve every previous numerical/source artifact.

target.require: DOMESTIC_OCCUPATION=Yes; at least one label in exactly one class. Keep overlap/unknown/non-domestic exclusions visible. Labels describe recorded contexts across the archive, not AD200 functions, markets or true absence.
target.timing: Whole-record archival contrast only; no role-date imputation or claim of contemporaneous occupation. Site date/phase flags reported for sensitivity; do not turn lack of dated evidence into absence.

matching: Operational OSGB-compatible X-easting/Y-northing metres. Use a documented trusted EPSG27700->WGS84 library pipeline, report installed/version/transform accuracy and missing-grid limits. Match nearest point of the full original lat/lon model grid using spherical distances, BEFORE checking land/allowed. No nearest-land rescue. Keep out-of-window, nonland and disallowed outcomes by class. No new source map required.
unit: Retain distinct source records and review blocks. Primary weights give each represented (model cell,class) unit total weight1; repeated excavations in that unit do not increase its mass. Mixed cells retain both classes and hence ties; never drop them to improve discrimination. These are observation units, not unique settlements or resident counts.
predictors: unchanged existing target centre intensity with historyL450 and spacingc0.35; no source label supplies a centre count
metrics: Report weighted pairwise-rank AUC (ties0.5), class/record/cell overlap and inclusion counts, plus 50km spatial-block diagnostics. This is conditional discrimination within a selected archive, not census accuracy, settlement completeness or political control. No label-based fitting, threshold optimization, offset fit, source reclassification or best-parameter selection.
coverage: Report region,fieldwork and investigated-AREA strata; AREA is investigation effort, not full settlement extent or population. Use preregistered AREA bins missing,positive<0.1ha,0.1–<1ha,>=1ha; source fieldwork strings remain explicit. Do not claim stratification removes excavation-selection bias.
uncertainty: Report membership/sampling sensitivity to coordinate offsets of0,±2km and±5km along each grid axis, retaining every scenario rather than picking best. These are sensitivity scenarios, not a calibrated location-error distribution. Old exact-association/point/name blocks are future leakage constraints, not independent transfer.
preparation_gate: Before scores, require at least30 represented cell/class units in each class in the original allowed-land footprint; report failure/inclusion counts if not met. Do not tune extent or threshold to pass.
decision: Diagnostic only; report all predictors and scenarios even if weak/reversed. A gain does not qualify world role assignment or complete S2. A failure prioritizes a role/observation mechanism rather than endless history-scale retuning.
consumers: Evidence for future typed residential/nucleated role allocation, then SAME resident/food/staffing/institution/control ledger. No administrator/market/garrison/actor from category alone. S1c actual history,S1d transfer,S1e joint rebuild and S3–S5 remain open.
